_meta.description: Control your external monitor's brightness and volume with your Mac keyboard. Tiny, invisible, free.
_title: Glint — DDC Display Control for Mac
a-mac-with-apple.3b5e98: A Mac with Apple silicon on macOS 13 Ventura or later. Intel Macs can keep using Glint 1.4.3 from the GitHub releases.
brightness-keys-change-only.fd9ba0: Brightness keys change only the display your cursor is on. Turn on sync mode and every screen moves together.
can-i-install-it.9ac23d: Can I install it with Homebrew?
does-glint-work-with.7c15a2: Does Glint work with my monitor?
does-it-conflict-with.a2c902: Does it conflict with other display apps?
glint-free-open-source.2f98fa:

glint-is-free-no.732582: Glint is free — no ads, no tracking, no subscription. If it earns a place on your Mac, you can help fund what comes next.
glint-talks-to-your.56a6d1: Glint talks to your monitor over DDC, the same channel its own buttons use. The backlight itself gets brighter or dimmer, not a gray layer on top.
how-do-i-get.d02e79: How do I get settings back after hiding the menu bar icon?
macos-13-or-later.9e06e8: macOS 13 or later on Apple silicon · notarized by Apple
most-external-monitors-support.ba4369: Most external monitors support DDC/CI. If your monitor has an OSD with brightness/volume controls, it almost certainly supports DDC. Works over HDMI, DisplayPort, and USB-C/Thunderbolt — including through USB-C hubs and docks. Glint automatically detects monitor audio routed through hubs.
no-electron-no-frameworks.5c8180: No Electron. No frameworks. Just your keyboard and your display.
open-glint-from-your.ed0a6d: Open Glint from your Applications folder (or Spotlight search for "Glint"). When the app detects it's being re-opened, it automatically shows the settings window.
possibly-if-two-apps.434ac2: Possibly — if two apps both intercept the same media keys, they may interfere. We recommend using one DDC controller at a time.
press-a-key-the.b211ad: Press a key. The monitor answers.
talking-to-a-monitor.1f2d61: Talking to a monitor over DDC needs hardware access the App Store sandbox blocks, so Glint ships as a direct download instead. Every release is notarized by Apple, and the source is open to read.
the-brightness-and-volume.07301d: The brightness and volume keys on your Mac finally work on your external display. Free, open source and under 1 MB.
the-real-backlight-not.41d1a9: The real backlight, not a filter
tiny-invisible-and-nothing.fe2e99: Tiny, invisible, and nothing to hide
to-intercept-media-key.1af391: To intercept media key events before macOS processes them, Glint uses a CGEventTap, which requires Accessibility permission. Without it, Glint can't detect brightness/volume key presses. This is a standard macOS security requirement for any app that reads keyboard input. After enabling access, you'll need to quit and relaunch Glint for it to take effect.
what-do-i-need.c6c81a: What do I need to run it?
when-audio-plays-through.9097d5: When audio plays through your monitor over HDMI, DisplayPort or USB-C, even through a hub, the volume keys drive its speakers. Headphones and AirPods work as they always have.
why-does-glint-need.8e8c95: Why does Glint need Accessibility access?
